variable_coverage.construction: For each annual observation t, Δ = TXPD_t − (TXR_t − TXR_(t−1)) − 0.35×PI_t; MVA1 is beginning market value of assets based on AT+((PRCC_Q×CSHO)−SEQ), with beginning AT/BVA substituted when MVA is missing. Divide Δ by MVA1. TXR meaning, statutory rate and exact fiscal-quarter matching remain source ambiguities.

TIME = observation year − 1988 (0 to 26). The paper does not state whether its observation year is the Compustat fiscal-year label (FYEAR) or calendar year of DATADATE; this anchor choice remains unresolved.

Table 6 Panel C reports no weighting scheme or weight variable; no weight input is specified.
The paper identifies a linear time-trend regression and an intercept but does not identify the estimator; this remains a blocking specification issue.
The source states 1st/99th percentile winsorization of Δ/MVA but does not specify the percentile pool; the scope ambiguity is retained below.

implementation_issues.description: The source’s TXR concept is inconsistent: Section 2.2 calls TXR a tax refund receivable, while Table 4 calls it tax reserves; the local field is labeled Income Tax Refund. Section 2.2 also prints 34% for fiscal years ended “1998 through 1992” and 35% for 1993-2014, while Table 4 applies .35×PI. The paper does not reconcile the definitions/rate schedule. The extracted baseline follows Table 4 but an exact Δ construction remains unresolved.
Table 6 describes a regression of Δ/MVA1 on a linear time trend, but does not name the estimator. No estimator is inferred from the reported table statistics.

The source defines TIME using “observation year” but does not identify whether this is Compustat FYEAR or calendar year of DATADATE. The period is 1988-2014; the exact year-field choice remains unresolved.

The paper states Δ/MVA is winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles but does not define whether cutpoints are pooled over all firm-years, calculated by year, or based on a different sample. This affects the outcome used in the trend fit.

The paper specifies PRCC_Q for MVA but does not state the exact quarter-to-annual match rule for beginning MVA1. The local quarterly close and annual date fields permit a candidate alignment; fiscal-year-end matching remains a construction choice.

The local routes are cataloged Compustat products, while the paper reports a 1988-2014 sample in a 2018 article. No evidence establishes that the current local vintage reproduces the paper’s historical coverage or values; report any later vintage differences if reconstruction proceeds.

evidence.quote: Therefore, we adjust cash taxes paid by the change (δ) in a firm’s tax refund receivable (TXR).
evidence.description: Section 2.2 describes TXR as a tax refund receivable; the PDF page was visually checked.

evidence.quote: We set τ equal to 34% for fiscal years ended 1998 through 1992 and to 35% for fiscal years ended 1993 through 2014 in our analyses.
evidence.description: Section 2.2 rate schedule as printed; 1998 through 1992 is the literal source text.

evidence.quote: MVA is computed as Compustat AT+((PRCC_Q*CSHO)-SEQ). BVA is equal to total assets (AT), and PTI is equal to pre-tax income (PI).
evidence.description: Table 1 states the raw Compustat scalar fields and defines BVA and PTI.

evidence.quote: We begin our examination of the effect of deleting loss firms and firms with negative CTE by constructing a sample of U.S. corporations from 1988 to 2014.
evidence.description: Section 3.1 source period and population.

evidence.quote: Following Dyreng et al. (2008), we consider firms to be U.S. corporations if Compustat data item FINC is equal to zero.
evidence.description: Footnote 14 first defines the U.S. corporation criterion.

evidence.quote: We eliminated non-corporate firms by deleting firms with a SIC code of 6798 (REITs)
evidence.description: Footnote 14. PDF cross-check (assigned PDF SHA-256 f60ae914bb0a1e3a0c0739214a0712a18f60889845db445430ca158e9ebbdb4e) confirms the remaining rules are names ending “-LP” containing “TRUST” and six-digit CUSIPs ending “Y” or “Z”; parsed JSON misreads these tokens.

evidence.quote: In addition, we delete observations where Compustat data item STKO is equal to 1 (subsidiary of a publicly traded company) or 2 (subsidiary of a non-publicly traded company), and when STKO is equal to zero (publicly traded company) but share price is missing.
evidence.description: Footnote 14 gives STKO code meanings and the share-price-missing rule.

evidence.quote: yielding a one-year sample of 124,514 firm-year observations with non-missing Δ/MVA1
evidence.description: Section 3.1 reports the one-year nonmissing measure count before the Table 6 minimum-observations filter.

evidence.quote: Δ is equal to cash taxes paid minus the change in tax reserves (TXPD – (TXRt – TXRt-1)) less the statutory rate times pre-tax book income (.35 * PI).
evidence.description: Table 4 defines the numerator and uses .35×PI.

evidence.quote: MVA1, MVA5, and MVA10 are equal to the sum of beginning market value of assets (AT+((PRCC_Q*CSHO)-SEQ)) over 1, 5, and 10 years, respectively. MVA is replaced with beginning book value of assets (BVA) when missing.
evidence.description: Table 4 defines the beginning-year scalar, raw inputs and BVA fallback.

evidence.quote: Δ/MVA and Δ/BVA are winsorized at 1 and 99%
evidence.description: Table 4 states the winsorization cutoffs but not the percentile universe.
